correctness.rationale: Split on whether a Poisson reset occurs during lag t; independence after a reset gives exact C(t)=exp(-r*t)Cov(g(A),g(A+t)) for stationary A~Exp(r). Since g(a)=T0∫w_q(s)e^-sa ds (Gamma density), Cov(e^-sA,e^-uA)=[r*s*u]/[(r+s+u)(r+s)(r+u)]>0. Tonelli yields strictly positive AC exponential density W(r+s), all moments finite; differentiation gives strict complete monotonicity. As s->0 W(r+s)~[T0*tau^q*mprime(r)/Gamma(q)]s^q, where mprime(r)=T0∫w_q(u)u/(r+u)^2 du>0. Watson/Laplace asymptotics give C~q*T0*tau^q*mprime(r)e^-rt t^(-q-1), with one-order remainder; tilt of the positive density yields LambdaPrime=-Var_t(lambda)<0 and Lambda-r=(q+1)/t+O(t^-2). The q=2 mean derivative yields the stated exponential-integral coefficient, positive from the integral. Independently evaluated exponential-age covariance by adaptive quadrature at r=.7,tau=1.2,q=2: normalized exact/asymptotic ratios at t=5,10,25,60 are 0.2684,0.4673,0.7098,0.8595, consistent with approach to one and not treated as proof; the analytic Laplace argument establishes all t and every q.
